Rice.overview: Rice is India's most widely grown cereal and the staple food crop of the Kharif season, grown mostly in flooded or well-watered fields.
Rice.conditions: Warm, humid weather with high rainfall or assured irrigation. Heavy clay or clay loam soils that hold water, pH about 5.5 to 7.
Rice.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before puddling. Basal dose of phosphorus and potash at transplanting; nitrogen split into three parts (basal, tillering, panicle initiation).
Rice.fertilizer_quantity: Roughly 105 kg urea, 150 kg single superphosphate and 40 kg muriate of potash per acre in total, nitrogen applied in 3 splits.
Rice.irrigation: Keep 2 to 5 cm of standing water from transplanting to the dough stage, with a drained spell at mid-tillering. Drain the field about 10 days before harvest.

Seedlings are moved to the puddled main field.
New shoots develop and the plant stand thickens.

Grains mature and the crop is cut.

Maize.overview: Maize is a versatile cereal grown for grain, poultry feed and industry, mainly in the Kharif season in India.
Maize.conditions: Warm weather with well-distributed rainfall and well-drained loamy soils. Waterlogging, even for a day or two, damages the crop.
Maize.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure at land preparation. Phosphorus and potash basal, nitrogen split in three parts.
Maize.fertilizer_quantity: About 105 kg urea, 150 kg single superphosphate and 27 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Maize.irrigation: Needs about 450 to 600 mm of water. Critical stages are knee-high, tasseling and silking; make sure drainage is available during heavy rain.

growth_stages.description: Male flowers appear at the top of the plant.
Silks emerge and pollination takes place.

Maize.pest_monitoring: Watch for fall armyworm, stem borer, leaf blight and stalk rot.
Maize.harvest: Harvest when husks turn dry and straw colored and kernels are hard with a black layer at the base. Dry cobs before shelling.

Cotton.overview: Cotton is India's major fibre crop, grown in Kharif on black and alluvial soils with a long, warm growing period.
Cotton.conditions: Warm climate, moderate rainfall and deep, well-drained black or alluvial soils. Needs plenty of sunshine during boll development.
Cotton.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Phosphorus basal; nitrogen and potash in splits at square formation and flowering.
Cotton.fertilizer_quantity: About 105 kg urea, 150 kg single superphosphate and 40 kg muriate of potash per acre across the season.
Cotton.irrigation: Critical stages are flowering and boll development. Avoid water stress then; avoid waterlogging at all stages.

Mature bolls split and lint is exposed.

Soybean.overview: Soybean is a protein and oilseed legume grown in Kharif, especially in central India.
Soybean.conditions: Warm, humid weather with moderate rainfall and well-drained loam soil. Waterlogging at germination and flowering is harmful.
Soybean.fertilizer: Seed treatment with Rhizobium culture helps nodulation. Apply phosphorus and potash basal; keep nitrogen low because the crop fixes its own.
Soybean.fertilizer_quantity: About 26 kg urea, 200 kg single superphosphate and 27 kg muriate of potash per acre, all as basal.
Soybean.irrigation: Mostly rain-fed. Give a protective irrigation if there is a dry spell at flowering or pod filling.

Groundnut.overview: Groundnut is an important oilseed and legume grown in Kharif on light soils.
Groundnut.conditions: Warm weather, moderate rainfall and well-drained sandy loam soil, which allows pegs to penetrate the soil easily.
Groundnut.fertilizer: Apply gypsum at flowering to improve pod filling. Treat seed with Rhizobium. Apply phosphorus and potash basal.
Groundnut.fertilizer_quantity: About 22 kg urea, 125 kg single superphosphate, 33 kg muriate of potash and about 200 kg gypsum per acre.
Groundnut.irrigation: Needs about 500 mm in total. Peg formation and pod development are critical, so avoid dry spells then.

Bajra.overview: Bajra (pearl millet) is a hardy millet suited to dry, warm regions of north-west and central India.
Bajra.conditions: Hot, dry climate with low to moderate rainfall and light, sandy or loam soils. Tolerates poor soils but not waterlogging.
Bajra.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Half of the nitrogen with phosphorus basal, half as top dressing.
Bajra.fertilizer_quantity: About 70 kg urea and 100 kg single superphosphate per acre in total.
Bajra.irrigation: Mostly rain-fed. One or two protective irrigations at tillering and flowering help in dry spells.

Jowar.overview: Jowar (sorghum) is a drought-tolerant cereal and fodder crop grown in Kharif and Rabi on medium to deep soils.
Jowar.conditions: Warm, semi-arid climate with moderate rainfall and well-drained medium black or loam soils.
Jowar.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Basal phosphorus and potash; split nitrogen between sowing and about 30 days.
Jowar.fertilizer_quantity: About 70 kg urea, 100 kg single superphosphate and 27 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Jowar.irrigation: Largely rain-fed. Protective irrigation at booting and grain filling improves yield in dry years.

Pigeon Pea.overview: Pigeon pea (arhar/tur) is India's main pulse crop of the Kharif season with a long, slow growth period.
Pigeon Pea.conditions: Warm, moderately humid climate, well-drained loam soil. Highly sensitive to waterlogging.
Pigeon Pea.fertilizer: Seed treatment with Rhizobium. Apply phosphorus basal; nitrogen only as a small starter dose.
Pigeon Pea.fertilizer_quantity: About 22 kg urea and 125 kg single superphosphate per acre, all basal.
Pigeon Pea.irrigation: Mostly rain-fed. Irrigate at flowering and pod filling if there is a long dry spell.

Moong.overview: Moong (green gram) is a short-duration pulse grown in Kharif that fits well in crop rotations.
Moong.conditions: Warm, moderately humid weather, moderate rainfall and well-drained loam soil. Avoid waterlogging.
Moong.fertilizer: Treat seed with Rhizobium. Apply a small starter nitrogen dose with phosphorus and potash at sowing.
Moong.fertilizer_quantity: About 18 kg urea, 125 kg single superphosphate and 13 kg muriate of potash per acre, all basal.
Moong.irrigation: Mostly rain-fed. One irrigation at flowering or pod filling in dry spells.

Sesame.overview: Sesame (til) is a small-seeded oilseed grown in Kharif and Zaid on light soils.
Sesame.conditions: Warm weather, low to moderate rainfall and well-drained sandy loam soil. Dislikes waterlogging.
Sesame.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Half nitrogen with phosphorus and potash basal.
Sesame.fertilizer_quantity: About 35 kg urea, 50 kg single superphosphate and 13 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Sesame.irrigation: Largely rain-fed. One irrigation at flowering or capsule formation can help.

Wheat.overview: Wheat is the main Rabi cereal of India, grown across the Indo-Gangetic plain in cool winter weather.
Wheat.conditions: Cool growing period, warmer weather at grain filling is harmful. Well-drained loam or clay loam soil with moderate moisture.
Wheat.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Phosphorus and potash basal; nitrogen half basal and half at first irrigation.
Wheat.fertilizer_quantity: About 105 kg urea, 150 kg single superphosphate and 27 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Wheat.irrigation: Needs 4 to 6 irrigations. Critical stages are crown root initiation (about day 21), tillering, jointing, flowering and grain filling.

Barley.overview: Barley is a hardy Rabi cereal used for food, fodder and malting.

Barley.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Basal phosphorus and potash; nitrogen half basal, half at first irrigation.
Barley.fertilizer_quantity: About 70 kg urea, 100 kg single superphosphate and 13 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Barley.irrigation: Needs 2 to 3 irrigations. Crown root, tillering and flowering are the critical stages.

Mustard.overview: Mustard is the main Rabi oilseed of northern India, grown in cool, dry winters.
Mustard.conditions: Cool weather with low rainfall, clear skies at flowering, well-drained loam soil.
Mustard.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure before sowing. Sulphur improves oil content; apply phosphorus, potash and sulphur basal, nitrogen split in two.
Mustard.fertilizer_quantity: About 70 kg urea, 100 kg single superphosphate, 13 kg muriate of potash and about 16 kg sulphur per acre.
Mustard.irrigation: Needs 2 to 3 irrigations. Rosette and pod filling stages are critical.

Chickpea.overview: Chickpea (chana) is the leading Rabi pulse, grown on residual soil moisture.
Chickpea.conditions: Cool, dry weather, light to medium well-drained soil, low rainfall. Excess moisture and frost at flowering reduce yield.
Chickpea.fertilizer: Treat seed with Rhizobium. Apply phosphorus and a small nitrogen starter dose basal.
Chickpea.fertilizer_quantity: About 18 kg urea and 125 kg single superphosphate per acre, all basal.
Chickpea.irrigation: Often rain-fed or 1 to 2 irrigations. Branching and pod filling are the critical stages; avoid over-irrigation.

Potato.overview: Potato is a major Rabi tuber crop grown in cool weather in the Indo-Gangetic plains.

Pumpkin.overview: Pumpkin is a Zaid and Kharif vegetable that spreads on the ground and stores well after harvest.
Pumpkin.conditions: Warm weather, well-drained loam soil rich in organic matter, steady moisture.
Pumpkin.fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure in pits. Phosphorus and potash basal; nitrogen split in two doses.
Pumpkin.fertilizer_quantity: About 70 kg urea, 100 kg single superphosphate and 27 kg muriate of potash per acre in total.
Pumpkin.irrigation: Irrigate every 7 to 10 days; reduce watering as fruits mature.

Summer Groundnut.overview: Summer groundnut is an irrigated Zaid oilseed crop grown after Rabi harvest.
Summer Groundnut.conditions: Warm weather with assured irrigation; sandy loam, well-drained soil.
Summer Groundnut.fertilizer: Apply gypsum at flowering. Treat seed with Rhizobium. Apply phosphorus and potash basal.
Summer Groundnut.fertilizer_quantity: About 22 kg urea, 125 kg single superphosphate, 33 kg muriate of potash and about 200 kg gypsum per acre.
Summer Groundnut.irrigation: Needs about 6 to 8 irrigations. Flowering, pegging and pod development are critical.
